column1: # Every loopback port this campaign has already bound, so "a port that has never
# been used" stops being something anyone has to remember.
# The rule this file exists to enforce: a run gets ports no earlier run had. Reusing
# one is not forbidden, but it must be DELIBERATE and it must be SAID — a report
# calling a reused port "new" is the failure this ledger prevents. `run_controlled.sh`
# refuses a port listed here unless --allow-reused-ports is passed, and every run
# records, per port, whether it was a first use or a reuse.
# Read the scope honestly: this ledger records what is KNOWN, and it was written
# after the fact. Absence from it is not proof a port was never bound on odb24 by
# anything — it means no run of THIS campaign recorded binding it. Production's own
# ports are listed because they are the ones that must never be touched at all.
# A port allocated to a run that never started is listed too, and said to be so.
# It was never bound, so it is not "used" in the sense the host would report — but
# a run's evidence is named against the ports it was launched with, and proposing
# one of them again as fresh is the same mistake in a quieter form.
# Maintained by hand and by commit. The runners cannot append to it: they execute
# from a throwaway export, so anything they wrote would be discarded with it. Adding
# the ports of a completed run is a deliberate edit before the next one is proposed.
